title: Why Good Enough Beats Perfect | Principles of Management Ep 24
description:
Why don't real managers pick the perfect option? In this animated lesson, Chai Corner is ready to open its sixth outlet, but the city has 4,000 streets and the good shops get rented in days. Checking every street, as the rational model says, would take a whole year.

You will learn what bounded rationality means (we try to be rational, but within limits), where the idea comes from (Herbert Simon: Administrative Behavior in 1947, the name in the 1950s, and the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1978), the three bounds on every decision (incomplete information, limited time, limited brain power), what satisficing means (satisfy + suffice: taking the first option that is good enough), and how it differs from the rational model, which optimises.

This is Episode 24 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 Four thousand streets, one outlet
0:22 What is bounded rationality?
0:31 Herbert Simon and the idea
0:47 The three bounds

2:06 Quick check
2:20 Recap
